messages:
sophie: FYI bringing up ceres-v0.2 (float32 -> q4_0) on staging last night. Nightly multilingual eval flagged large quality swings for zh->en and ja->en.

eval-bot: regression alert triggered for ceres-v0.2 q4_0 on staging. Metrics summary: zh->en BLEU -3.4, ja->en BLEU -4.7, COMET -0.22 vs float32 baseline. Full eval run: job 67420.

jihoon: can you paste a minimal repro (input + tokenization diff) so we can see if it's a tokenizer or decoding issue?

sophie: quick repro below. looks like an unexpected ZERO-WIDTH SPACE (U+200B) is showing up in token sequence for quant run but not in fp32.

```
# reproducer (staging tokenizer instance)
src = "这是一个测试。"
# float32 tokenizer.encode(src) -> [ ... ]  (no U+200B)
# q4_0 tokenizer.encode(src)    -> [ ..., 8203, ... ]  # 8203 == U+200B inserted between han graphemes
# observed decoded outputs:
# float32: "这是一个测试。"
# q4_0:    "这是一个测试。"  <-- extra ZWSP inside sentence
```

maia: interesting. we saw something vaguely similar with streaming + prefix cache when we brought up a different model, but not as consistent. two hypotheses: (1) quant kernel changes boundary merging for certain multigram merges (affects tokenizer post-processing), or (2) KV-cache restore path inserts a soft-boundary marker when a chunk ends inside a grapheme cluster.

maia: quick experiment idea: rerun eval with prefix/kvcache disabled and with streaming turned off. If metric delta vanishes, it's an interaction rather than pure quantization.

akshay: +1. also try q8_per_channel if that's available; if q8 matches fp32 then it's likely quant-kernel induced. I'll queue both.

sophie: triggered two reruns:
- job 67421: q4_0, kvcache=false, streaming=false
- job 67422: q4_0, kvcache=true, streaming=true (original config)
- job 67423: q8_per_channel, kvcache=true, streaming=true

infra-bot: job results posted:
- 67421 (kvcache=false): zh->en BLEU -0.3, ja->en BLEU -0.4 vs float32
- 67422 (kvcache=true): zh->en BLEU -3.6, ja->en BLEU -4.8 vs float32
- 67423 (q8_per_channel): zh->en BLEU -0.2, ja->en BLEU -0.1 vs float32
Links: https://ci.redwood/job/67421, /67422, /67423

jihoon: that pretty strongly implicates kvcache + q4 kernel interaction. when kvcache is disabled quantized run is close to baseline.

maia: can you dump the kvcache snapshot around the boundary? I want to diff token sequences before/after restore. Also include the raw bytes of the last tokens in the previous chunk — might reveal a byte-level insertion.

sophie: pasted small hex dump and token id stream for a failing sample in job 67422 artifacts. key snippet shows restore inserted 0xE2 0x80 0x8B (UTF-8 for U+200B) between two han characters when chunk reassembly happened.

akshay: root cause hypothesis: q4 microkernel uses a different subword fusion heuristic for the last partial token in a chunk; the kvcache restore logic treats that as a boundary and injects a boundary marker for streaming. under fp32 or q8 the kernel produced the full merged token so no marker was injected.

jihoon: action items I can take:
- bisect quant kernel change set that touched subword merge logic (assign to me)
- add invariant test: kvcache restore roundtrip should not change decoded bytes for given input chunks
- add a small regression test that runs with an explicit U+200B detection (fail on unexpected insertions)

maia: I'll craft a minimal unit test that simulates chunked encode/decode + kvcache restore and runs across quant backends. Put it in repo: tests/eng-ml/tokenization/kvcache_roundtrip_test.py.

sophie: I'll hold ceres-v0.2 canary and remove q4_0 from the staging rollout until we have a fix. Pushing a mitigation: default to q8_per_channel for ceres on streaming routes.

akshay: putting rollout hold now, noted in the release checklist. :thumbsup:

jihoon: filing GH issue now with reproducer, job ids, and suggested bisect range: https://github.com/redwood-inference/coreruntime/issues/4291

sophie: thanks all — will update this thread when bisect narrows down commit. short-term: kvcache toggle + q8 fallback seems to restore eval parity.

eval-bot: closing alert for job 67421 (kvcache disabled) since metrics are within drift thresholds. Will re-open if new regressions appear.

maia: fyi leaving a note to check other CJK-heavy datasets (news, subtitles) — if this pattern repeats across corpora we should consider a targeted e2e test in the nightly suite.

sophie: agreed, adding to next sprint.
